name: Awesome Cursor Rules Bundle
description: A curated collection of high-value developer rules for Cursor, sourced from PatrickJS/awesome-cursorrules.

prompts.name: React Router v7
prompts.content: Use route modules as the primary boundary for UI, loaders, actions, metadata, and error boundaries. Utilize `loaders` for fetching deterministic data and `actions` for mutations/form submissions. Store shareable state in the URL search parameters and keep ephemeral UI state local. Avoid global state for data belonging to route loaders. Enforce type-checking on all `loader` and `action` return values.

prompts.name: React/Zustand
prompts.content: Write state management logic using Zustand. Provide guidance on creating modular stores, implementing middleware, handling persistence, and exporting state selectors effectively. Avoid deeply nested state structures and separate UI components from global state stores to optimize React renders.

prompts.name: Python Best Practices
prompts.content: Adopt a modular `src/` architecture and break functionality into distinct files (models, services, utilities). Always include strict typing annotations (including `None` for returns) and PEP 257-compliant docstrings. Use `pytest` for all testing within a `./tests` directory instead of `unittest`. Enforce early returns/guard clauses, use `Ruff` for linting, and utilize `uv` for modern dependency management.

prompts.name: Python 3.12 + FastAPI
prompts.content: Build async RESTful APIs using FastAPI and Python 3.12 features. Use Pydantic V2 for strict data validation and serialization. Implement dependency injection for database sessions and configuration. Keep route handlers small and delegate core business logic to dedicated service layers. Leverage Python's modern typing system (e.g., `|` for Union types) introduced in recent versions.

prompts.name: HTMX + Go Basic Setup
prompts.content: Structure a Go web application returning server-rendered HTML snippets meant for HTMX consumption rather than JSON endpoints. Maintain standard Go project layouts (e.g., `/cmd` and `/internal`). Ensure HTML templates are clean and semantic, embedding HTMX attributes directly. Keep handlers lightweight and properly handle HTTP caching and partial view renders.
